newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton invites Israel's Netanyahu for visit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton invites Israel's Netanyahu for visit.

text.p: President Bill Clinton invited Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to visit the United States to discuss developments in the Middle East, an Israeli spokesman said on Tuesday.
The message was delivered by U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross who returned to the region on Monday to help Israel and the PLO seal a Hebron deal.
"In the message, the U.S. president writes that he respects the decisions which the prime minsiter made in order to advance the peace talks," Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement.

"The president added that he wants to conduct a comprehensive strategic dialogue with Prime Minister Netanyahu regarding regional developments. The president invited the prime minister to meet at the beginning of the new year," he said.
Israel and the PLO were hammering out final details on Tuesday of an agreement to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinians after months of U.S.-brokered negotiations.
Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat were expected to meet on Wednesday to seal the long overdue deal.

Netanyahu has been under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, to honour the Hebron withdrawal and other aspects of a 1995 Israel-PLO peace deal reached during the term of Israel's previous government.

Netanyahu and Clinton last met in October at a U.S. arranged summit with Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan after a wave of violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip in which 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
